chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever confesses during stripping, or frightening, or imprisonment, or threat, then there is no Hadd (fixed penalty) upon him.

key_terms.تَجْرِيدٍ: Stripping (of clothes) as a form of pressure or humiliation
key_terms.حَدَّ: Hadd (fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia)

ai.seo_question: Does a confession made under duress or threat count for imposing the Hadd penalty in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates a fundamental principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding the nullification of Hadd penalties when confession is extracted under duress, specifically listing stripping (tajrid), fear (takhwif), imprisonment (habb), and threats (tahdid). It reflects the Imams' emphasis on voluntary consent for legal accountability, ensuring that punishments are not imposed on those coerced by physical or psychological pressure. This ruling underscores the fairness inherent in Islamic criminal law, protecting individuals from self-incrimination under force.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bandar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, form his father, from Abu Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘
The one who confesses during the stripping, or frightening, or imprisonment, or imposition of a Penalty (Hadd), so there is no Penalty (Hadd) upon him (Due to being under duress/pressure)’.
